title: promotion-guards prints 'genuine fast-forward' for a force-push rewind of main
summary: The main-is-fast-forward-of-dev job asserts only 'git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/dev' - that main's new HEAD is a commit dev holds. It never looks at where main WAS, so it cannot distinguish a forward promotion from a backwards rewind. A force-push moving main to an older commit that is still on dev satisfies the ancestor test and the job prints 'main's HEAD (...) is reachable from dev: genuine fast-forward.' The job is named 'main landed via fast-forward from dev' and measures only the 'from dev' half; the 'fast-forward' half is unmeasured and affirmatively claimed. github.event.before (and github.event.forced) are available on push events and unused.
description:
Raised as a hypothesis by the lore-cli session on 2026-09-15 via opum-agent: an assertion written inline in a workflow run: block can have no tests by construction, so whatever correctness it has is unmeasured. This job is exactly that shape - it is entirely inline in promotion-guards.yml, has no test surface, and only executes on a real push to main, so no run has ever exercised it except a real promotion.

Measured with a scratch bare repo (dev with c1..c4; main starting at c2), running the assertion verbatim on a fresh clone checked out at main's pushed SHA:
  A. genuine promotion, push dev tip c4 over main c2   -> GREEN 'genuine fast-forward'   (correct)
  B. force-push rewind, main c4 -> c1 (older, on dev)  -> GREEN 'genuine fast-forward'   (WRONG)
  C. button-style merge commit pushed to main          -> RED                            (correct)
Scenario B erased two commits of shipped history from main and the guard affirmed it as genuine.

This is lore-cli's generalisation landing exactly: both halves of prove-it-rejects (C) and prove-it-accepts (A) pass, and the gate is still wrong, because the missing question is what its success message CLAIMS versus what it measured. A reader who sees 'genuine fast-forward' after an incident stops looking - which is worse than no message, since the rewind is precisely the state someone would be investigating.

Severity is bounded and should be stated honestly: force-push to main is already tier-3 forbidden by the fleet operating model and needs a human, so this is defense-in-depth failing open rather than a live exposure. That is also what the job is FOR - the comment in the file calls it 'defense in depth'. A defense-in-depth guard that affirms the thing it is defending against is the defect.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The job asserts main moved FORWARD as well as from-dev: github.event.before is an ancestor of the new HEAD (skipping the check when before is the all-zero SHA, i.e. branch creation)
github.event.forced is surfaced - a forced push to main is reported as such rather than absorbed into a green result, whatever the ancestor tests say
The success message states both facts it measured (moved forward from <before>, and is a commit dev holds) rather than the single word genuine
The assertion is extracted from the inline run: block into a script with a suite that drives it over a fixture repo, so it has tests at all - scenarios A, B and C above are the minimum cases
Proven both directions with versions recorded: red on the rewind fixture with the rewind-specific message, green on a genuine fast-forward, and the other jobs green on both

implementationNotes: Reproduction script kept at scratchpad ff.sh during the session; it is ~25 lines of bash over a scratch bare repo and is worth re-writing into scripts/test/ rather than recovered - the scratchpad is session-scoped.

Watch the zsh trap when re-deriving this by hand: "$SHA:refs/heads/main" is mangled by zsh, which reads :r as a variable modifier and silently pushes to a garbage refspec. Two runs of this proof produced confident-looking GREEN/RED output from pushes that had all failed. Use ${SHA}:refs/heads/main, or run it under bash.

Neither promotion-guards job is a required check, by design (the file explains why: requiring them would make the one correct promotion path unpushable). So this fix changes what a human reads after a promotion, not what blocks one. That is the point - the message is the entire product of this job.
Related in kind to OMARK-57, which is the same question (claim versus measurement) asked of the federated checkers' success messages.

REPLICATED INDEPENDENTLY in lore-cli, filed there as LCLI-514, 2026-09-15. Its ci.yml carries a main-is-fast-forward-of-dev job asserting merge-base --is-ancestor $GITHUB_SHA origin/dev with no read of event.before - same defect, different repo. lore-cli measured it in a scratch repo asserting the constructed state before the verdict: guard says GREEN on a rewind where a real fast-forward check (is-ancestor c4 c2) says RED. Its own comment calls it 'the guard that matters most for this repo specifically: main carries zero branch rules here', so the failing-open case is worse there than here. Two independent instances means the shape probably came from the shared opum-doc promote-dev-to-main runbook, which promotion-guards.yml cites - fixing it here without routing the shape back leaves the other copies wrong.

TEST-AUTHORING TRAP for the extracted assertion (same note on OMARK-57): scope assertions to the emitted verdict, not to the surrounding prose. This job's success string will grow to state two measured facts (moved forward from <before>, and is a commit dev holds); assert those two facts structurally rather than string-matching the sentence, or the test becomes a tripwire on wording.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION, drafted 2026-09-15 at opum-agent's request (it ruled: one correct version written by the session that measured the defect, handed to the other seven owners as text, no session edits a sibling). Recorded here in full because the scratchpad it was built in is session-scoped. Proven 8/8 on a scratch bare repo: accepts a real promotion; rejects the rewind the old guard called genuine; names a forced push distinctly; rejects a commit dev never held; accepts branch creation without claiming forward movement; accepts an unchanged re-push; fails when the previous HEAD cannot be resolved; refuses to report at all when BEFORE_SHA is unset. Script body follows verbatim in the next note.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Asserts that main's new HEAD (a) moved FORWARD from where main was, and
# (b) is a commit dev already held. The original guard checked only (b) and
# reported "genuine fast-forward" on a rewind - two commits could come off
# main and it said green (opum-marketplace OMARK-58, lore-cli LCLI-514).
#
# Inputs, so this is runnable outside Actions and therefore testable at all:
#   BEFORE_SHA  - github.event.before  (all-zero when the branch is created)
#   FORCED      - github.event.forced  ("true"/"false")
set -euo pipefail

ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
before="${BEFORE_SHA:?BEFORE_SHA not set - refusing to report on an unmeasured previous position}"
forced="${FORCED:-false}"

git fetch --no-tags --quiet origin dev
head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
dev_sha="$(git rev-parse origin/dev)"

# (b) came from dev. Unchanged from the original assertion.
if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$head_sha" "$dev_sha"; then
  echo "::error::main's new HEAD ($head_sha) is not a commit dev ever held. This is not a promotion from dev - a merge button or a direct commit produces this. Do not push over it until the anomaly is understood; see opum-doc docs/runbooks/promote-dev-to-main.md, Rollback."
  exit 1
fi

# A forced push to main is never needed for a fast-forward, so its presence is
# the anomaly regardless of what the ancestor tests say. Checked separately so
# the operator is told WHICH thing happened.
if [ "$forced" = "true" ]; then
  echo "::error::main was FORCE-PUSHED ($before -> $head_sha). A fast-forward promotion never requires --force. Force-push to main needs your own user's direct authority; see opum-doc docs/runbooks/promote-dev-to-main.md."
  exit 1
fi

# (a) moved forward. This is the half the original never measured.
if [ "$before" = "$ZERO" ]; then
  movement="created at $head_sha (main did not exist before this push, so there is no previous position to compare)"
elif ! git cat-file -e "${before}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::main's previous HEAD ($before) cannot be resolved in this clone, so forward movement CANNOT be proven. Treat as an anomaly, not as a pass - an object that is gone is usually one a rewrite orphaned."
  exit 1
elif [ "$before" = "$head_sha" ]; then
  movement="unchanged at $head_sha"
elif git merge-base --is-ancestor "$before" "$head_sha"; then
  movement="moved forward $before -> $head_sha"
else
  echo "::error::main was REWOUND or diverged: its previous HEAD ($before) is not an ancestor of its new HEAD ($head_sha). Commits that were on main are no longer on main. This passes an is-ancestor-of-dev check, which is why that check alone was not enough. Do not push over it; see opum-doc docs/runbooks/promote-dev-to-main.md, Rollback."
  exit 1
fi

# Says the two things it measured, not "genuine fast-forward" generally.
echo "main $movement, and its HEAD is a commit dev holds (dev tip $dev_sha). Fast-forward from dev confirmed on both counts."

Workflow job calling the script above (the point of the extraction is that the assertion is now reachable by a test at all):
  main-is-fast-forward-of-dev:
    name: main landed via fast-forward from dev
    if: github.event_name == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: main must have moved forward, and from dev
        env:
          BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
          FORCED: ${{ github.event.forced }}
        run: ./scripts/ci/assert-main-fast-forward.sh
fetch-depth: 0 is load-bearing twice over: the shallow default has neither the previous HEAD nor enough history for either is-ancestor test.

SEVERITY CORRECTION, 2026-09-16, and it raises this task's priority. This task and every message I sent about it said opum-marketplace was the defense-in-depth case because main is protected - 'a force-push rewind would still have to get past the required contexts'. THAT INFERENCE IS WRONG. quest-cli caught it on its own copy and it generalises; I then measured all five supposedly-protected repos and they are identical.

  gh api repos/opum-ai/opum-marketplace/rulesets/22669384
    name: require-ci-on-main | enforcement: active | bypass_actors: []
    rules: required_status_checks ONLY
    contexts: check - manifests, Tracker integrity, lore check
    non_fast_forward rule: ABSENT     deletion rule: ABSENT

Same for opum-agent, opum-doc, quest-cli and opum-cli-e2e - all five carry required_status_checks and nothing else, no non_fast_forward, no deletion, zero bypass actors.

Why protected=true is inert HERE SPECIFICALLY: required status checks gate a push on the PUSHED COMMIT'S OWN check history, not on which direction the branch moved. Check runs attach permanently to a SHA, so any commit previously promoted to main already carries three green contexts by construction - promotion is what put them there. Rewinding main onto such a commit is pushing a commit the ruleset is already satisfied by. Nothing named non_fast_forward exists to refuse it. Worse than quest-cli's framing for us: our three contexts also run on pushes to dev, so an arbitrary dev commit that was never on main likely carries them too, which widens the set of rewind targets the ruleset accepts.

The sharp version, quest-cli's: the ruleset backs up exactly the half of the guard that already works and provides nothing for the half that is broken. Assertion 1 (a foreign or merge-button commit) IS genuinely double-covered - such a commit has no prior green contexts. Assertion 2 (the rewind) has no second line at all.

So on this specific failure mode opum-marketplace is not in a different class from the rules=0 repos. Priority moved To Do/Medium -> To Do/High to match.

Epistemic status, stated because this task is about claims outranging their measurements: this is strong inference from two API reads (rules/branches/main and the full ruleset), not an empirical test. I have not force-pushed main to confirm and will not - that is tier 3 and destructive. The absence of non_fast_forward in BOTH endpoints is the evidence; /rules/branches/main aggregates classic branch protection and rulesets into the same rule-type vocabulary, so its absence there covers the classic-protection case too.

PROCESS LESSON, same day, and it is the same defect class this task documents. I measured 'main rules=1 protected=true' (correct) and reported 'therefore a rewind still has to get past the required contexts' (wrong). The object I measured was WHETHER a rule exists; the object my claim was about was WHETHER THAT RULE REFUSES THIS PUSH. One gh api call apart, and I shipped the inference to four repositories as if it were the measurement. This is precisely the gate defect at human scale - the job measured containment and its name claimed fast-forwardness. When passing a severity signal onward, pass the rule TYPES, which are a fact, not the conclusion 'you are covered', which is an inference about a specific attack.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION v2 supersedes the v1 recorded above. DO NOT IMPLEMENT v1. Three changes, all from peer review of the draft:

(a) THIRD ASSERTION, from opum-fleet. v1 passed a stale-local-dev partial promotion - ODOC-193, 'git push origin dev:main' off a stale local dev instead of 'origin/dev:main'. That moves main forward to a commit dev genuinely holds, so v1's forward check AND containment check both went green while less was delivered than intended. VERIFIED against v1 before accepting the report: built main=c3 / dev=c4 on a scratch repo and v1 printed 'Fast-forward from dev confirmed on both counts', exit 0. v2 adds 'git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/dev'. It is a WARNING, NOT A RED, deliberately: dev legitimately advancing between the promotion push and the CI run produces a non-zero count with nothing wrong, and a red there would fire on correct behaviour - which is the exact defect that pushes a later author to weaken a check to get it green. This repo is directly exposed: our own CLAUDE.md cites ODOC-193 and requires the origin/dev:main form.

(b) HEADER STATING WHAT THE JOB IS NOT, from opum-web. It runs on push, after the fact, and REPORTS - it does not block. Whether anything refuses a bad push is the branch rules, a separate mechanism. Without this a later session reads a green promotion job as a gate that stopped something. Also states it speaks only to GIT SHAPE: where a promotion includes a deploy or publish step, green here is not 'the promotion succeeded' (opum-web's OWEB-3: a commit produced no production deployment at all while git looked fine).

(c) Containment error now names the unrecoverability - main stops being an ancestor of dev and can never fast-forward again - because opum-web reports the merge button is fully reachable there with allow_auto_merge=true and zero protection.

Proven 11/11 on a scratch bare repo: the original 8 cases plus exact-promotion-leaves-nothing-behind, partial-promotion-warns-but-stays-green, and partial-promotion-names-the-commit-left-behind. Script body verbatim in the next note.

Provenance worth keeping: the guard had three independent gaps found by three different sessions against one copied shape that had never had a test anywhere - containment without forward movement (here), the job name claiming more than the assertion measured (lore-cli), and forward-and-contained but stale (opum-fleet).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# WHAT THIS IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. This runs on push to main, after the fact.
# It REPORTS; it does not block. Whether anything actually refuses a bad push
# depends on your repo's branch rules, which are a separate mechanism - check
# `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/main` and do not assume a green
# run here means something was stopped. It also speaks only about GIT SHAPE: if
# your promotion includes a deploy, a publish or a propagation step, green here
# is not "the promotion succeeded".
#
# Three properties, each asserted and reported separately so a failure names
# which one broke. The original guard asserted only #2 and printed "genuine
# fast-forward", claiming #1 and #2 together while measuring #2 alone
# (opum-marketplace OMARK-58, lore-cli LCLI-514, quest-cli, opum-web OWEB-8).
#
#   1. main moved FORWARD          - github.event.before is an ancestor of HEAD
#   2. main's HEAD CAME FROM dev   - HEAD is contained in origin/dev
#   3. main IS dev, not part of it - nothing left behind (warning only, see below)
#
# Inputs, so this is runnable outside Actions and therefore testable at all:
#   BEFORE_SHA - github.event.before (all-zero when the branch is created)
#   FORCED     - github.event.forced ("true"/"false")
set -euo pipefail

ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
before="${BEFORE_SHA:?BEFORE_SHA not set - refusing to report on an unmeasured previous position}"
forced="${FORCED:-false}"

git fetch --no-tags --quiet origin dev
head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
dev_sha="$(git rev-parse origin/dev)"

# ASSERTION 2 - came from dev. Unchanged from the original; do not drop it.
if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$head_sha" "$dev_sha"; then
  echo "::error::main's new HEAD ($head_sha) is not a commit dev ever held. A merge button or a direct commit produces this, and it is unrecoverable: main stops being an ancestor of dev and can never fast-forward again. See opum-doc docs/runbooks/promote-dev-to-main.md, Rollback."
  exit 1
fi

# A forced push to main is never needed for a fast-forward, so its presence is
# the anomaly regardless of what the ancestor tests say. Separate, so the
# operator is told WHICH thing happened.
if [ "$forced" = "true" ]; then
  echo "::error::main was FORCE-PUSHED ($before -> $head_sha). A fast-forward promotion never requires --force. Force-push to main needs your own user's direct authority."
  exit 1
fi

# ASSERTION 1 - moved forward. The half the original never measured.
if [ "$before" = "$ZERO" ]; then
  movement="created at $head_sha (main did not exist before this push, so there is no previous position to compare)"
elif ! git cat-file -e "${before}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "::error::main's previous HEAD ($before) cannot be resolved in this clone, so forward movement CANNOT be proven. Treat as an anomaly, not as a pass - an object that is gone is usually one a rewrite orphaned."
  exit 1
elif [ "$before" = "$head_sha" ]; then
  movement="unchanged at $head_sha"
elif git merge-base --is-ancestor "$before" "$head_sha"; then
  movement="moved forward $before -> $head_sha"
else
  echo "::error::main was REWOUND or diverged: its previous HEAD ($before) is not an ancestor of its new HEAD ($head_sha). Commits that were on main are no longer on main. This passes an is-ancestor-of-dev check, which is why that check alone was not enough."
  exit 1
fi

# ASSERTION 3 - main IS dev, not merely part of it. WARNING, NOT A FAILURE, and
# the distinction is deliberate: dev legitimately advancing between the
# promotion push and this run produces a non-zero count with nothing wrong, so a
# hard fail here would cry wolf. It catches ODOC-193 - promoting a STALE LOCAL
# dev with `git push origin dev:main` instead of `origin/dev:main`, which moves
# main forward to a commit dev really holds and so satisfies 1 and 2 while
# delivering less than intended. Raised by opum-fleet, where main is the ref the
# fleet installs opum-workflow from, so a short promotion ships a stale plugin
# with everything green.
behind="$(git rev-list --count "${head_sha}..${dev_sha}")"
if [ "$behind" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::warning::main is $behind commit(s) BEHIND dev after this push. If dev advanced after the promotion, this is expected and fine. If not, this was a PARTIAL promotion - the classic cause is pushing a stale local dev (git push origin dev:main) instead of the remote-tracking ref (git push origin origin/dev:main), ODOC-193. Left behind:"
  git log --oneline --no-decorate "${head_sha}..${dev_sha}" | sed 's/^/::warning::  /'
  completeness="but is $behind commit(s) behind dev (see warning)"
else
  completeness="and is dev's tip exactly, with nothing left behind"
fi

# States the three things it measured, not "genuine fast-forward" generally.
echo "main $movement; its HEAD is a commit dev holds (dev tip $dev_sha), $completeness. Reported, not enforced - see this script's header."

MAINTENANCE TRAP in the v2 script, from lore-web (LWEB-88) after implementing it. The FORCED branch and the REWOUND branch are near-redundant in production: a rewind of main is essentially always forced, so github.event.forced fires first and the REWOUND message becomes near-dead code in CI logs. Both still earn their place - FORCED defaults to false when the script is run by hand, and a rewind performed via the API or a delete-and-recreate need not set it. The trap is a future author noticing the rewind branch never appears in real logs and 'simplifying' it away, which would restore exactly the defect this task exists for. Do not reorder or merge those two branches; if anything, add a test asserting the rewind branch fires with FORCED=false, which our suite already does.

MUTATION-CHECKING THE SUITE, from lore-web, worth copying when OMARK-58 is implemented here. Green tests against a correct script prove nothing about the tests. lore-web reverted its script to the old one-liner and re-ran: 6 of 10 cases went red, and the containment case correctly STAYED green, because the old one-liner preserves that behaviour. A suite that went red on containment too would have been testing the script's identity rather than its properties. That asymmetry is the evidence the suite measures the right thing - a uniformly-red mutation run is a weaker result, not a stronger one. Same technique applies to OMARK-57: mutate check-federated-pins.mjs back to market.plugins.length and confirm ONLY the count/name assertions go red.

LIMIT OF ASSERTION 3, from opum-cli-e2e, to be stated at the gate rather than left to the reader. 'dev legitimately advanced between the push and the run' and 'partial promotion from a stale local dev' are INDISTINGUISHABLE at the moment the job runs. The warning cannot tell them apart. That is fine for a warning and would be a defect in a red - which is the positive case for keeping it soft, stronger than 'it might cry wolf'. Say so in the emitted text so a reader does not assume the check discriminates.

WIRING IS A SEPARATE OBJECT FROM LOGIC, from opum-web (OWEB-8, PR #14, run 35022915616, guard-proof job 104562849569: 5 cases / 12 assertions all pass, all eight checks green on the same SHA). It committed a proof harness as its own CI job, which proves the SCRIPT'S LOGIC. It does not prove the WORKFLOW WIRING - that BEFORE_SHA/FORCED are actually populated from the github.event context, and that fetch-depth: 0 actually supplies main's previous HEAD. The guard job is gated on push-to-main, so on a PR it reports 'skipping' and neither has ever executed. The failure lands in the expensive direction: with a shallow checkout the script hits the git cat-file branch, reports an unresolvable previous position and EXITS 1, reddening a good promotion on the one event everyone is watching, having never run before. So when OMARK-58 is implemented here, the honest status until the first real dev-to-main push is: script logic proven, wiring unproven. Do not report it as proven end-to-end before then, and expect the first promotion to be the wiring test.

REAL-REPO PROOF EXISTS ELSEWHERE, so do not re-derive it: opum-web run 35022915616 is CI-confirmed on a real repository, and quest-web (QWEB-46, PR #64) and lore-web (LWEB-88, PR #107) both implemented and mutation-checked. quest-web's mutation: 10 of 11 red, survivor 'rejects a commit dev never held' - the one property the old one-liner preserves. lore-web removing assertion 3 alone: exactly 2 of 11 red, the two completeness cases. Both asymmetries are the evidence the suites test properties rather than identity. quest-web also adapted the fetch to an explicit refspec (+refs/heads/dev:refs/remotes/origin/dev) rather than bare 'git fetch origin dev', so origin/dev existing does not depend on git's opportunistic remote-tracking update under actions/checkout's narrowed refspec - bare worked in its runs but nothing asserted it. Take that adaptation.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION v3 supersedes v2. One change, from opum-web (OWEB-8 PR #15), and it is the same wrong-object defect this task documents, found inside the fix for it. v2's unresolvable-previous-HEAD branch named only the alarming cause - 'an object that is gone is usually one a rewrite orphaned' - so a SHALLOW CHECKOUT, which is a workflow misconfiguration, would be reported as a DAMAGED main. v3 splits the diagnosis on 'git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository'.

The exit code is deliberately UNCHANGED in both branches. Weakening it to make the false red less likely would have been the wrong fix: an unmeasured previous position is still not a pass, and the assertion keeps its full strength. Only the object the error names changes.

VERIFIED the branch is reachable that way rather than taking it on report: cloned --depth 1 from a scratch bare repo, ran the guard's own 'git fetch --no-tags origin dev', and measured is-shallow-repository still true afterwards with the previous HEAD still unresolvable. So the guard's fetch does not deepen the clone and the shallow case genuinely holds.

opum-web's two new test cases are a MATCHED PAIR - same missing object, opposite diagnosis - and each asserts the ABSENCE of the other's wording, because a single over-broad message would pass a presence-only test in both directions. Same reason it split the rewind into forced and unforced. Take both cases, not just the fix. Its proof is now 7 cases / 19 assertions.

Suite here still 11/11 after applying the change; the existing unresolvable case runs on a full clone and correctly takes the else branch.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# WHAT THIS IS, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. This runs on push to main, after the fact.
# It REPORTS; it does not block. Whether anything actually refuses a bad push
# depends on your repo's branch rules, which are a separate mechanism - check
# `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/rules/branches/main` and do not assume a green
# run here means something was stopped. It also speaks only about GIT SHAPE: if
# your promotion includes a deploy, a publish or a propagation step, green here
# is not "the promotion succeeded".
#
# Three properties, each asserted and reported separately so a failure names
# which one broke. The original guard asserted only #2 and printed "genuine
# fast-forward", claiming #1 and #2 together while measuring #2 alone
# (opum-marketplace OMARK-58, lore-cli LCLI-514, quest-cli, opum-web OWEB-8).
#
#   1. main moved FORWARD          - github.event.before is an ancestor of HEAD
#   2. main's HEAD CAME FROM dev   - HEAD is contained in origin/dev
#   3. main IS dev, not part of it - nothing left behind (warning only, see below)
#
# Inputs, so this is runnable outside Actions and therefore testable at all:
#   BEFORE_SHA - github.event.before (all-zero when the branch is created)
#   FORCED     - github.event.forced ("true"/"false")
set -euo pipefail

ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
before="${BEFORE_SHA:?BEFORE_SHA not set - refusing to report on an unmeasured previous position}"
forced="${FORCED:-false}"

git fetch --no-tags --quiet origin dev
head_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
dev_sha="$(git rev-parse origin/dev)"

# ASSERTION 2 - came from dev. Unchanged from the original; do not drop it.
if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$head_sha" "$dev_sha"; then
  echo "::error::main's new HEAD ($head_sha) is not a commit dev ever held. A merge button or a direct commit produces this, and it is unrecoverable: main stops being an ancestor of dev and can never fast-forward again. See opum-doc docs/runbooks/promote-dev-to-main.md, Rollback."
  exit 1
fi

# A forced push to main is never needed for a fast-forward, so its presence is
# the anomaly regardless of what the ancestor tests say. Separate, so the
# operator is told WHICH thing happened.
if [ "$forced" = "true" ]; then
  echo "::error::main was FORCE-PUSHED ($before -> $head_sha). A fast-forward promotion never requires --force. Force-push to main needs your own user's direct authority."
  exit 1
fi

# ASSERTION 1 - moved forward. The half the original never measured.
if [ "$before" = "$ZERO" ]; then
  movement="created at $head_sha (main did not exist before this push, so there is no previous position to compare)"
elif ! git cat-file -e "${before}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
  # Same missing object, two very different causes, and the guard used to name
  # only the alarming one - reporting a damaged main when the real fault was a
  # missing fetch-depth: 0 (opum-web). The exit code is deliberately unchanged:
  # an unmeasured previous position is still not a pass. Only the diagnosis
  # differs. Verified that the guard's own `git fetch --no-tags origin dev` does
  # NOT deepen a shallow clone, so this branch really is reachable that way.
  if [ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = "true" ]; then
    echo "::error::THIS CHECKOUT IS SHALLOW, so main's previous HEAD ($before) was never fetched and forward movement cannot be proven. This is a fault in the WORKFLOW, not in the promotion: the job needs actions/checkout with 'fetch-depth: 0'. main is very probably fine - fix the checkout and re-run before treating this as a damaged branch."
  else
    echo "::error::main's previous HEAD ($before) cannot be resolved in this clone, so forward movement CANNOT be proven. The clone is NOT shallow, so this is not a fetch-depth problem. Treat as an anomaly, not as a pass - an object that is gone in a full clone is usually one a rewrite orphaned."
  fi
  exit 1
elif [ "$before" = "$head_sha" ]; then
  movement="unchanged at $head_sha"
elif git merge-base --is-ancestor "$before" "$head_sha"; then
  movement="moved forward $before -> $head_sha"
else
  echo "::error::main was REWOUND or diverged: its previous HEAD ($before) is not an ancestor of its new HEAD ($head_sha). Commits that were on main are no longer on main. This passes an is-ancestor-of-dev check, which is why that check alone was not enough."
  exit 1
fi

# ASSERTION 3 - main IS dev, not merely part of it. WARNING, NOT A FAILURE, and
# the distinction is deliberate: dev legitimately advancing between the
# promotion push and this run produces a non-zero count with nothing wrong, so a
# hard fail here would cry wolf. It catches ODOC-193 - promoting a STALE LOCAL
# dev with `git push origin dev:main` instead of `origin/dev:main`, which moves
# main forward to a commit dev really holds and so satisfies 1 and 2 while
# delivering less than intended. Raised by opum-fleet, where main is the ref the
# fleet installs opum-workflow from, so a short promotion ships a stale plugin
# with everything green.
behind="$(git rev-list --count "${head_sha}..${dev_sha}")"
if [ "$behind" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "::warning::main is $behind commit(s) BEHIND dev after this push. If dev advanced after the promotion, this is expected and fine. If not, this was a PARTIAL promotion - the classic cause is pushing a stale local dev (git push origin dev:main) instead of the remote-tracking ref (git push origin origin/dev:main), ODOC-193. Left behind:"
  git log --oneline --no-decorate "${head_sha}..${dev_sha}" | sed 's/^/::warning::  /'
  completeness="but is $behind commit(s) behind dev (see warning)"
else
  completeness="and is dev's tip exactly, with nothing left behind"
fi

# States the three things it measured, not "genuine fast-forward" generally.
echo "main $movement; its HEAD is a commit dev holds (dev tip $dev_sha), $completeness. Reported, not enforced - see this script's header."

RESIDUAL, from quest-cli, not fixed: absence assertions can be PUNCTUATION-COUPLED. It had asserted absence of "fetch-depth: 0'" - with a trailing quote lifted from the message it came from - and a combined-message mutant writing "fetch-depth: 0." walked through its whole suite. Ours asserts the full phrase THIS CHECKOUT IS SHALLOW rather than a punctuated fragment, and the combined-message mutant is caught, so the specific defect is not present here. The residual is that grep -qF is case-sensitive: a mutant differing only in casing would evade the absence assertion. Judged not worth another change - a casing-only mutation is not a plausible edit - but recorded so the next author knows it was considered rather than missed.

LATE FINDING from lore-web (LWEB-90), arrived after this task closed, recorded because it is mechanically checkable and would otherwise be lost with the session. Three times in one evening it added a property to ONE half of a matched pair and not the other: liveness on the new case but not the older one it was paired with; a precondition assertion on the shallow fixture but not the full-clone one. Its diagnosis is more specific than 'check both halves': the defect is that THE HALF BEING ACTIVELY WRITTEN GETS THE NEW PROPERTY AND THE HALF THAT ALREADY EXISTED AND PASSES DOES NOT. A pair created in one sitting will not have this; a pair where one half is older than the property always will. The mechanical check it proposes: when adding an assertion to one case of a pair, DIFF THE TWO CASES' ASSERTION SETS. Worth applying to this repo's own suite before the next change to it - our matched pairs were built in one sitting so they are currently symmetric, which is luck of timing, not a property anything enforces.

Not verified here: I have not diffed our pairs' assertion sets, and lore-web's measurement (making its full-clone path shallow reddens 9 of 12, the predicted scope) is its own and was not reproduced in this repository.

LIMIT ON MY OWN RE-RANKING, flagged by lore-web and accepted. I moved 'adversarial re-run against a differently-shaped fixture' above mutation-checking on lore-web's causal claim that in all five fixture instances the re-run is what caught it. lore-web has since qualified its own evidence and the qualification is right: it established that the re-runs DID catch five of five, not that an adversarial re-run RELIABLY catches this class - in its own case the re-run that found it was performed for an unrelated reason (checking my claim, not auditing its fixture). So the honest split for anyone writing this up: 'mutation-checking as I was reading it missed a bad fixture' is measured and solid; 'adversarial re-runs catch this class' is five-for-five and encouraging, and is not the same thing as a mechanism. The first deserves more confidence than the second. Note this sits alongside the correction already recorded above - mutation-checking is NOT blind to a bad fixture, it produces a lone surviving mutant, which is a quiet signal I was not reading for.

KNOWN DEFECT IN SHIPPED CODE, NOT FIXED - left for the next session, from quest-cli, arriving during session renewal. scripts/ci/assert-main-fast-forward.sh line ~34 fetches with '2>/dev/null', so when the fetch fails the operator gets MY PARAPHRASE and git's own most specific fact is discarded. Confirmed present by grep; the failing path was measured earlier in this task and does emit a correct, annotated exit 1, so this is a diagnostic-quality defect rather than the silence class - the verdict is right and the content is lossy.

quest-cli's generalisation, which is better than 'also print stderr': the split is not about missing OBJECTS, it is that A WRAPPER WHICH PARAPHRASES A TOOL'S ERROR OWES THE OPERATOR THE ORIGINAL, and the sites where that matters are exactly the sites where a non-zero exit means FAILURE rather than ANSWER. That is a typing distinction and therefore mechanical. Its implementation splits one helper into two: one for questions where non-zero is a legitimate answer (is-ancestor, cat-file -e) where discarding stderr is correct, and one for operations where non-zero is a failure, which returns stderr and quotes git verbatim.

Applied here that means: keep 2>/dev/null on the cat-file -e probe, where a non-zero exit is the answer; drop it on the fetch, capture stderr, and append 'git said: <text>' to the error. Also note quest-cli's ordering rule for the new case - assert PRESENCE of ::error:: BEFORE any absence assertion, per the silence finding. It measured reverting its equivalent site reddening exactly 1 of 14.

Not verified here: I have not made the change or measured it in this repository. The grep confirming 2>/dev/null is present is the only measurement behind this note.
finalSummary:
Delivered in PR #114, squashed to dev at 580e6dc. The guard is now scripts/ci/assert-main-fast-forward.sh with a 15-case proof suite wired into check - manifests so it runs on every PR; promotion-guards.yml calls the script.

Three assertions with three separate messages, kept separate on purpose - adding forward-movement as a REPLACEMENT for containment would have traded a known blind spot for a new one while looking like a fix. (1) main moved forward, via github.event.before. (2) main's HEAD is contained in origin/dev, unchanged from the original. (3) main IS dev, not merely part of it - a WARNING, never a red, because dev advancing after a correct promotion and a partial promotion are structurally indistinguishable at the moment the job runs, and the emitted text now says so. Forced pushes are named distinctly. The success line states the three facts measured with their SHAs; 'genuine fast-forward' is gone, because that phrase asserted the conclusion the job was named for while measuring half of it.

BOTH DIRECTIONS PROVEN THROUGH CI, with run ids. GREEN: e38ee97, run 35024329153, all three required checks green and all 15 cases visible in the job log rather than inferred. RED: ba584b0, run 35024391678, throwaway PR #115 closed unmerged - dropping the fetch refspec made check - manifests fail at 'Promotion guard has a passing proof suite' with 'wanted exit 1, got 128 - a different non-zero is a different failure', while lore check and Tracker integrity stayed green on that same SHA. Versions: node 24.20.0 local and CI, quest 0.7.1, git 2.x on macOS and ubuntu-latest.

Mutation-checked five ways, selectively: drop assertion 1 reddens 6 while containment and completeness stay green; drop assertion 3 reddens 5; collapse both unresolvable causes into one over-broad message reddens exactly the 2 matched-pair cases; drop only the fetch refspec reddens exactly 1, the shallow case; replace the file:// clone with a plain path reddens exactly 1 with FIXTURE BROKEN. A uniformly red mutation run would have been the weaker result.

WHAT IS NOT PROVEN, stated rather than covered by 'verified': the workflow WIRING, in EITHER direction. Nothing here measures that BEFORE_SHA/FORCED are populated from the github.event context or that fetch-depth: 0 is present at runtime, because the guard job is gated on push-to-main and reports skipping on every PR. This repository's first real promotion will buy the accept direction only; the reject direction would mean deliberately pushing a bad state to main, which is the thing the guard exists to prevent and will not be manufactured. Language taken from lore-web.

Peer contributions, each verified here before adoption rather than taken on report: assertion 3 and warning-not-red (opum-fleet); its discrimination limit (opum-cli-e2e); the shallow/full split, matched-pair test design, the negative-assertions-are-satisfied-by-silence finding and the abort trap (opum-web); the explicit fetch refspec, which turned out to be load-bearing for reachability rather than cleanup, and the assert-what-the-fixture-constructed rule (quest-web); the production-shape fixture correction and the scoped wiring assertion (lore-web); the --depth-ignored-for-local-path trap (opum-fleet).

MY OWN ERROR IN THIS TASK, recorded because it is the task's own subject: I verified the shallow branch's reachability against a fixture cloned --branch dev, which creates origin/dev for free and made the branch reachable whether or not the fetch was right. I measured is-shallow still true and the previous HEAD still unresolvable - both correct, both independently reproduced - but those are PRECONDITIONS of the branch, not REACHABILITY of it, and the failure sat between them. I then distributed that unreachable fix to six repositories. My own implementation was correct only because I had adopted the refspec for an unrelated reason. Correct implementation, broken distribution, same session, same hour, while attending specifically to this failure mode.
